title: Grateful Dead Live at Hollywood Palladium on 1972-09-10
source: SBD > [MR > C > DAT(s) ??] > CDR(s) > DAE > SHN

ai_review.summary: Excellent soundboard capture of a high‑energy 1972 show highlighted by a scorching Dark Star and an extended, spooky He's Gone.
ai_review.review: The recording is a pristine soundboard mix that lets every instrument shine – the guitars are especially forward and clear. Musically the concert bursts with intensity from the opening jam through to the soaring Dark Star (where Phil’s bass is in the zone) and a haunting, extended outro on He's Gone, making it a standout performance for Deadheads.

ai_rating.rationale: The majority of reviews are glowing (5‑star) and praise both the superb soundboard recording and the high energy of the performance, with only one low rating that reflects personal taste rather than objective flaws.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Crisp, well‑balanced mix; guitars (Jerry and Bob) are prominent, with a slightly higher Bobby level noted but not detrimental. No reported dropouts or muddiness.

show_quality.setlist_flow: Intense opening jam sets a high‑octane tone, flowing smoothly into extended improvisations; Dark Star and He's Gone provide the centerpiece of the night.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Takes two strong solos on He's Gone; his guitar is clear and forward in the mix.
band_member_comments.Phil: In the zone during Dark Star, delivering powerful bass work around the 12:30 mark.
band_member_comments.Bob: His rhythm guitar sits higher in the mix than usual, adding extra bite to the early jam.
